**Review of the search ad (UK)**

**Sentence by sentence**
- "Tea Subscription UK": plain description of the product, fine.
- "Monthly loose leaf tea.": a product fact, fine.
- "If your box isn't right, we'll make it right.": **problem.** This is a soft, implied guarantee. A customer could reasonably read it as a promise of a replacement, refund or remedy. The brand policy only backs up the ability to pause or cancel any time. It has no returns, refund or satisfaction promise, and the ad gives no conditions. The wording is also vague about what "right" means.
- "Free UK delivery on orders over £25.": matches the approved claim exactly, with the threshold stated. Fine.

**Other checks**
- No health, green, superlative, statistic, testimonial or urgency claims.
- No paid-creator or affiliate content, so no label is needed.
- Style is plain, with no AI clichés.

**Fix:** Remove the line, or replace it with something the brand can back up, such as "Pause or cancel any time." If the brand does operate a remedy policy, get its terms approved and state the main conditions.
